input_note: BGR, 0-255, NOT normalised — the /255 is inside the graph, hence `no_preprocess` on both inputs. Two inputs means two positionally-matched calibration directories.

outputs.flow: 1x2x384x512 dense displacement field, in MODEL pixels — the decoder rescales to source-image pixels
outputs.note: Iteration counts are export-time constants (1 at 1/16 scale, 8 at 1/8), so the refinement loops are fully unrolled and the graph carries no control flow.

quantisation: set_all_nodes_int16, and this one is not a precaution — see rejected_builds. int8 compiles fine and is unusable.

licence.tier: UNRESOLVED — recipe only, do not redistribute the .hbm
licence.detail: The code is Apache-2.0 and, unusually, the pretrained weights are committed inside that same repository — which normally makes the root licence cover them. The data chain is what stops it. `neuflow_mixed.pth` is trained on FlyingThings3D and Sintel, and FlyingThings3D's terms of use read in full: 'This dataset is provided for research purposes only and without any warranty. Any commercial use is prohibited.' Those terms say nothing at all about models trained on the data — they neither extend the restriction to derivatives nor grant permission for them. Under this repo's own rule, silence is not permission, so this sits where OSNet sits: the recipe is public, the binary is not. Sintel is a second open question, reported as CC BY 3.0 by some sources and CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 by others. If you need a redistributable flow model, retrain the architecture on data you can account for — the recipe is the part that matters and it is here.

toolchain.note: The host HBDK and the board HBRT must match; 3.7.0 host pairs with 4.0.5 board.

cosine.note: A is ONNX against torch: cosine 1.000000 and EPE 0.0000 px after the Conv+BN fusion and init_bhwd. B and C are deliberately not the gate here — see task_metric. The compiler's own output cosine for the int8 build was 0.9954 and that build is unusable, which is the entire lesson of this recipe.

task_metric.name: endpoint error against SYNTHESISED ground truth, plus a static-pair noise floor
task_metric.protocol: Optical flow is one of the few tasks where exact ground truth needs no dataset: translate an image by a known integer number of pixels and the correct field is that constant everywhere. Run known 2-16 px shifts (dropping a 48 px border so the wrap-around does not pollute the measurement) and take the median EPE. Separately, feed the SAME frame twice: whatever comes back is pure noise, so it measures the floor directly.
task_metric.threshold: median EPE within ~0.1 px of the float model across the shift range, and a static-pair floor below ~0.1 px
task_metric.measured: float ONNX: 0.025 px floor, 0.036-0.076 px EPE. int16: 0.070 px floor, 0.055-0.081 px EPE. int8: 1.936 px floor, 1.61-2.15 px EPE.
task_metric.note: On real frame pairs, the int8 build's cosine against float collapses to 0.02 where the true displacement is ~0.05 px. Fast pixels look fine at 12% relative error; slow ones are entirely noise.

measured.note: S100P, hrt_model_exec perf, thread_num 1, min of 3 runs on a board gated against its own recorded numbers.

rejected_builds.name: int8 (compiler default)
rejected_builds.why: A FLAT ~1.9 px noise floor: a 2 px displacement and a 16 px displacement both come back with about the same error, so the relative error looks acceptable (12%) on fast pixels and the slow ones are pure noise. The compiler reported 0.9954 output cosine for it — a field with a 60 px dynamic range absorbs 2 px of noise without moving a cosine much. int16 costs 34% latency and recovers essentially float accuracy. THE RULE: a head that regresses a physical quantity must be scored in that quantity's units.

graph_rewrites.why: The released checkpoints are not fused; upstream fuses at load time in infer.py. An export that skips it is not the network anybody measured.
graph_rewrites.verified: ONNX vs torch cosine 1.000000, EPE 0.0000 px.

graph_rewrites.why: It precomputes the correlation lookup's linspace/meshgrid into constants for one fixed resolution. Without it those trace as live Range/Shape ops and the graph carries dynamic shapes.
graph_rewrites.verified: After onnxslim: 890 nodes, opset 17, no Shape/Range/Sqrt remaining — fully static.

graph_rewrites.why: Tracing the half-precision demo path exports a half graph the toolchain will not take.

board_verification.note: Compiled and board-verified: 19.45 ms BPU, 26.4 ms end to end, with the synthesised-shift EPE above. Two things worth repeating for the next model: do NOT time a loop that reads from a compressed .npz — the first attempt measured 87.5 ms end to end, of which 66 ms was re-decompressing the images each iteration; and of the 26.4 ms, 6.3 ms is preprocessing two frames with a hand-written bilinear resize, which OpenCV or NEON would cut.
board_verification.not_done: The `sintel` and `things` checkpoints were not tried (the shipped build uses `mixed`), and no resolution other than 512x384 was compiled — hbm size and latency scale with input AREA.
